data.name: Thailand
data.summary: Thai residents (more than 180 days a year) pay progressive tax up to 35% on Thai income and, since 2024, on foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 whenever it is remitted to Thailand (pre-2024 income stays exempt even if remitted). Gains on shares sold on the Stock Exchange of Thailand are exempt; Thai dividends can be taxed at a final 10%. Foreign dividends and gains kept abroad are not taxed. Inheritance tax applies at 5% for children on amounts above THB 100 million received from each deceased; gifts from parents to children above THB 20 million a year are taxed at 5%. Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa holders in the wealthy categories are exempt on remitted foreign income.

regimes.name: Thai tax resident
regimes.description: Progressive 0-35% on Thai-source income and on foreign income earned from 2024 when remitted to Thailand.
regimes.eligibility: Present in Thailand for more than 180 days in the calendar year. Foreigners need a long-stay visa (e.g. LTR, Thailand Privilege/Elite, retirement).

capital_gains.summary: No separate CGT: gains are ordinary income at up to 35%, but gains on SET-listed shares sold through the exchange and on mutual fund units are exempt. Foreign gains are taxed only if remitted to Thailand; under Revenue Department orders Paw. 161/2566 and 162/2566, foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 is taxable when remitted in that or any later year.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: SET-listed shares sold on the exchange: exempt. Thai mutual fund units: exempt. Foreign income earned before 2024: exempt when remitted. Capital losses cannot offset gains.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Remittance basis: the 35% rates on foreign shares and foreign real estate ASSUME the gain is remitted to Thailand (Revenue Department orders Paw. 161/2566 and 162/2566: foreign income earned from 1 January 2024 is taxable when brought into Thailand in that or any later year). Gains kept abroad are not taxed (0%). The scoring uses the remitted case.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains on Thai real estate sold by individuals are taxed through a special withholding computation on the appraised value with deductions for years held, plus specific business tax if held under 5 years (not verified in detail; local real estate rate left null). Digital-asset gains through licensed Thai exchanges exempt 2025-2029.

sources.title: Thailand - Individual - Taxes on personal income

capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign shares and foreign real estate: 35% top marginal rate applies only to gains earned from 2024 and remitted to Thailand; 0% if kept abroad. SET shares exempt. Private (unlisted Thai) company sale: ordinary income up to 35%. Local real estate: special regime not verified, left null.
capital_gains.professional_trader: No separate trader test for SET shares (exempt in any case). Foreign trading gains are subject to the same remittance rule.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Taxed on remittance only (income earned from 1 January 2024). Credit for foreign tax only where a tax treaty allows it.

dividends.summary: Thai dividends bear a 10% withholding tax that residents may treat as final (or include in income and claim a dividend credit). Foreign dividends are taxed at progressive rates up to 35% only if earned from 2024 and remitted to Thailand; credit for foreign tax only under a treaty.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: First THB 150,000 of net income exempt (general band).
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Remittance basis: the 35% foreign_gross_rate ASSUMES the dividends are remitted to Thailand (Paw. 161/2566 and 162/2566). Foreign dividends kept abroad are not taxed (0%). Thai dividends: 10% final withholding regardless.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign tax credit is available only under a double tax treaty (61 treaties, including the US).

sources.title: Thailand - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 10% final WHT election. Foreign: 35% top rate if remitted (0% if kept offshore), with treaty-based credit.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 10% final WHT on dividends paid to foreign companies not doing business in Thailand (treaty-reducible).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 20%; Thai holding company dividends from Thai companies may be partly or fully exempt (not verified).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land and building tax on property values (rates not verified). Foreigners cannot generally own land; condominium units are allowed within the foreign quota.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax (Inheritance Tax Act B.E. 2558, 2015) is levied on the heir: the value above THB 100 million received from each deceased person is taxed at 5% for descendants and ascendants (10% for others); spouses are exempt. Gifts from parents to their legitimate children are exempt up to THB 20 million per child per year; the excess is taxed at 5% as income tax on the recipient.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: THB 100 million per heir per testator; spouse exempt; gifts to children THB 20 million per child per year.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Taxable property includes immovable property, securities, bank deposits, registered vehicles and prescribed financial assets; it covers worldwide property for Thai nationals and Thai-domiciled foreigners, but only Thai property for other foreigners (general rule from the Act, not verified in this session).
inheritance.spouse_note: An inheritance received by the deceased's spouse is outside the Inheritance Tax Act B.E. 2558 whatever its size (Thai law-firm summaries; the statute section was not located). Other heirs pay 5% (descendants, ascendants) or 10% above THB 100 million.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts from parents to legitimate children above THB 20 million per child per year are taxed at 5% (income tax on the donee, not aggregated with other income).
inheritance.foreign_assets: For foreign nationals not domiciled in Thailand, only Thai-situs property is believed to be in scope (not verified).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Heir-based: applies to Thai nationals, and to foreigners domiciled in Thailand (worldwide property) or receiving Thai property (not verified).

regimes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Wealthy Global Citizen / Wealthy Pensioner
regimes.description: LTR visa holders in these categories are exempt from Thai tax on overseas income remitted to Thailand (BOI list of privileges: 'tax exemption for overseas income'; Royal Decree No. 743, not opened).
regimes.eligibility: Wealthy Global Citizen: at least USD 1 million in assets and USD 500,000 invested in Thai government bonds, Thai companies or Thai property before applying. Wealthy Pensioner: age 50+, passive income of USD 80,000 a year (or USD 40,000-80,000 plus USD 250,000 investment). Spouse and children under 20 (up to 4 dependants). Visa 5 years, renewable for 5.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign gains remitted to Thailand are exempt for LTR holders; Thai gains taxed as standard.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: LTR visa holder in the Wealthy Global Citizen or Wealthy Pensioner category: overseas income is exempt even when remitted, so the 0% foreign rates do not depend on keeping money abroad.
open_questions: Exact scope of the LTR overseas-income exemption (whether dependants are covered) not verified from the Royal Decree.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Overseas income (including gains) exempt even if remitted; Thai items as standard.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends remitted to Thailand are exempt for LTR holders.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: LTR visa holder in the Wealthy Global Citizen or Wealthy Pensioner category: overseas income is exempt even when remitted, so the 0% foreign rates do not depend on keeping money abroad.
dividends.rate_basis: Overseas income exempt; Thai dividends 10% final.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present in Thailand for more than 180 days in aggregate in a calendar year.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident visa (Wealthy Global Citizen)
routes.requirements: USD 1 million in assets plus USD 500,000 invested in Thailand; dependants included; 5+5 years.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident visa (Wealthy Pensioner)
routes.requirements: Age 50+, USD 80,000 a year of passive income (or USD 40,000+ with a USD 250,000 investment).

corporate.summary: 20% CIT (graduated rates for small companies). Pillar Two: QDMTT, IIR and UTPR from fiscal years beginning 1 January 2025 (Top-up Tax Decree, 26 December 2024). 10% WHT on dividends to foreign companies.
corporate.special_zones: Board of Investment (BOI) incentives and Eastern Economic Corridor (not researched).

income.name: Thailand

income_tax.summary: Residents (180 days or more in a calendar year) pay progressive tax from 0% to 35% on net income; employment income gets a 50% expense deduction capped at THB 100,000 plus a THB 60,000 personal allowance. Foreign income earned from 2024 is taxable when remitted to Thailand. Employees pay 5% social security on wages up to THB 17,500 a month (max THB 875).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Section 33 applies to employees (foreign employees with work permits included). Independent contractors without a Thai employer pay no mandatory contribution; whether foreigners may join voluntary Section 40 was not verified from an official SSO page. Self-employed (section 40(2) etc.) may deduct actual expenses or a standard 10-60% depending on the business; the exact rate per activity was not listed on the PwC page.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Bracket thresholds are on net income after the 50% employment expense deduction (max THB 100,000) and allowances (THB 60,000 taxpayer, THB 60,000 non-filing spouse). The social security cap is THB 17,500 x 12 = THB 210,000 of wages.

sources.title: Thailand - Individual - Taxes on personal income
Thai Social Security wage ceiling increase 2026 (KPMG Tax News Flash 157)

open_questions: Whether foreigners on non-work visas can join voluntary Section 40 (not confirmed on an official SSO page).
Standard deduction percentage for freelance/consulting income (section 40(2)/(8)) not listed on the PwC page.

regimes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Highly-Skilled Professional
regimes.description: BOI Long-Term Resident visa for highly skilled professionals working in a targeted industry. The Revenue Department's LTR tax presentation states the 17% rate is a flat withholding rate on employment income, granted to Highly-Skilled Professionals (LTR-H) who work for a company operating in a targeted industry (as defined under the Competitiveness Enhancement for Target Industries Act, the Investment Promotion Act or the Eastern Economic Corridor Act). Conditions: the employer must notify the Area Revenue Office on the prescribed form and the 17% applies from the date the office acknowledges it; tax withheld at 17% can be treated as final, provided the holder does not claim a refund or credit; the holder still files PND 95 and needs a Tax ID. The separate exemption for foreign-sourced income belongs to the Wealthy Global Citizen, Wealthy Pensioner and Work-from-Thailand Professional categories, not to LTR-H.
regimes.duration_note: First permission 5 years, extendable by another 5 if still qualified. USD 80,000 a year average over the past two years; USD 40,000-80,000 needs extra proof (e.g. a master's degree in science or technology). Needs health insurance of USD 50,000 or Thai social security or USD 100,000 on deposit for 12 months. Fee THB 50,000.

sources.title: Tax Essentials for LTR Visa Holders (Revenue Department presentation)

open_questions: The Revenue Department slides do not state a cap or minimum for income taxed at 17%; whether it covers bonuses and benefits in kind was not checked.

It does not change tax: a holder staying 180 days or more in a year is a Thai tax resident, taxed on foreign income earned from 2024 only when remitted to Thailand.
regimes.duration_note: Five-year validity, 180 days per stay with an extension option. THB 500,000 in funds. Income test not given on the opened page.

succession.name: Thailand
succession.summary: Thailand has no forced heirship: a will can leave the estate to anyone (Civil and Commercial Code Book VI). Foreign nationals domiciled in Thailand come under Thai succession law, and Thai land follows Thai law. There is no general trust law and foundations are for public benefit, and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.family_claims: No court-ordered family provision found; the Code gives statutory heirs (including spouse and parents) shares only on intestacy.
succession.foreign_law_note: Act on Conflict of Laws B.E. 2481: movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile at death and immovables follow the law of their location. There is no right to choose a national law; a foreigner domiciled in Thailand falls under Thai law. A foreign will is usually valid in form. In Narathiwat, Pattani, Yala and Satun, Islamic law applies to Muslims on family and succession.
succession.trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. Thailand has no general trust law; the Trust for Transactions in Capital Market Act B.E. 2550 allows business trusts only. A foreign trust is not clearly recognised. Foundations (Civil and Commercial Code ss. 110-136) serve charitable or public purposes and need registration; a family foundation is not available. Foreigners who inherit land must dispose of it (Land Code s. 93).
open_questions: Sources disagree on the section numbers of the Conflict of Laws Act (s. 37 vs 38-42); check the official text.
Confirm Land Code s. 93 time limit and Islamic Law Act B.E. 2489 scope.
Confirm no forced-heirship rule in the Code from a primary text (my reading rests on the 'no' reputation of the system).

immigration.name: Thailand
immigration.summary: No free movement for EU citizens. Every passport can use the Long-Term Resident visa: Wealthy Global Citizen (USD 1 million of assets with USD 500,000 invested in Thailand), Wealthy Pensioner (age 50+, USD 80,000 a year of passive income), Work-from-Thailand or Highly-Skilled (USD 80,000 a year). Cheaper options are the Destination Thailand Visa for remote workers (THB 500,000 in savings), the 10-year O-X retirement visa for 50+ (THB 3 million deposit, eligible-country list) and Thailand Privilege membership (from THB 650,000).
immigration.naturalisation: Thai citizenship by naturalisation generally needs permanent residence first (after 3 consecutive years on annual extensions), then about 5 years, Thai language and an income test; PR quota is about 100 per nationality a year. Figures come from secondary guides.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Thailand generally allows dual nationality; not confirmed on an official source in this run.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Wealthy Global Citizen
routes.summary: Ten-year visa for people with USD 1 million of assets, USD 500,000 of which is invested in Thailand.
routes.requirements: At least USD 1 million in assets in the applicant's name (may include the Thai investment) and at least USD 500,000 already invested in Thai government bonds (5+ years remaining), Thai-registered companies or Thai property. Plus one of: health insurance of at least USD 50,000, Thai social security, or USD 100,000 in a bank account held 12+ months. Initial 5 years, extendable 5 more if qualifications are still met; investment must be maintained. 10-year multiple-entry visa; no work permit included.
routes.investment_options: USD 500,000 in Thai government bonds, direct investment in Thai companies, or Thai property.
routes.fees_note: THB 50,000 per person for the 10-year visa when collected in Thailand; no BOI fee for direct online applications; higher via embassies or VFS.
routes.physical_presence: No minimum stay stated by BOI; 90-day reporting applies; tax residence at 180 days
routes.processing_time: Not stated on the BOI page.
routes.family: Spouse and children under 20, maximum 4 dependants; each needs USD 50,000 insurance, Thai social security or USD 25,000 held 12+ months.
routes.tax_note: Thailand taxes foreign income remitted in the year earned from 2024; staying over 180 days makes you tax resident. The LTR carries a personal income tax exemption on foreign income for some categories (not verified here).

routes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Wealthy Pensioner
routes.summary: Ten-year visa for people aged 50+ with USD 80,000 a year of passive income, or USD 40,000 plus a USD 250,000 Thai investment.
routes.requirements: Age 50 or over; unearned income of at least USD 80,000 a year (pension, rent, realised gains, dividends, interest; salary does not count). If income is USD 40,000-79,999, an existing USD 250,000 investment in Thai bonds, a Thai company or Thai property is also required. Plus one of: health insurance of at least USD 50,000, Thai social security, or USD 100,000 in a bank account held 12+ months. Initial 5 years plus 5.
routes.investment_options: Alternative: USD 40,000 minimum income plus USD 250,000 invested in Thailand.
routes.fees_note: THB 50,000 per person for the 10-year visa when collected in Thailand; no BOI fee for direct online applications; higher via embassies or VFS.
routes.physical_presence: No minimum stay stated by BOI; 90-day reporting applies; tax residence at 180 days
routes.processing_time: Not stated on the BOI page.
routes.family: Spouse and children under 20, maximum 4 dependants; each needs USD 50,000 insurance, Thai social security or USD 25,000 held 12+ months.
routes.tax_note: Staying over 180 days makes you tax resident.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Work-from-Thailand Professional
routes.summary: Ten-year visa for remote workers earning USD 80,000 a year from a large foreign employer.
routes.requirements: Average personal income of at least USD 80,000 a year over the past two years (USD 40,000-79,999 with a master's degree or higher); contract with a listed company, a private company with 3+ years and USD 50 million combined revenue over 3 years, or its wholly owned subsidiary. Plus one of: health insurance of at least USD 50,000, Thai social security, or USD 100,000 in a bank account held 12+ months. No Thai work permit is granted.
routes.fees_note: THB 50,000 per person for the 10-year visa when collected in Thailand; no BOI fee for direct online applications; higher via embassies or VFS.
routes.physical_presence: No minimum stay stated by BOI; 90-day reporting applies; tax residence at 180 days
routes.processing_time: Not stated on the BOI page.
routes.family: Spouse and children under 20, maximum 4 dependants; each needs USD 50,000 insurance, Thai social security or USD 25,000 held 12+ months.
routes.tax_note: Staying over 180 days makes you tax resident.

routes.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa - Highly-Skilled Professional
routes.summary: Ten-year visa with a work permit for specialists in BOI target industries earning USD 80,000 a year.
routes.requirements: Average personal income of at least USD 80,000 a year over the past two years (USD 40,000-79,999 with a master's degree in science or technology); employment contract in a BOI-targeted industry or proven expertise in specified fields. Plus one of: health insurance of at least USD 50,000, Thai social security, or USD 100,000 in a bank account held 12+ months. Work permit fee THB 3,000 a year.
routes.fees_note: THB 50,000 per person for the 10-year visa when collected in Thailand; no BOI fee for direct online applications; higher via embassies or VFS.

routes.processing_time: Not stated on the BOI page.
routes.family: Spouse and children under 20, maximum 4 dependants; each needs USD 50,000 insurance, Thai social security or USD 25,000 held 12+ months.

routes.name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
routes.summary: Five-year multiple-entry visa for remote workers and 'soft-power' participants, up to 180 days per entry.
routes.requirements: Remote workers (workcation) or soft-power activity participants (e.g. Thai boxing, cooking, courses, medical treatment); proof of THB 500,000 in funds held at least three months; 180 days per entry, one 180-day extension in Thailand for THB 1,900; fee THB 10,000 at some embassies but varies by embassy (e.g. USD 400 in Washington); apply from outside Thailand via thaievisa.go.th. Remote work for a Thai employer is not allowed. Details from embassy pages and secondary reports; the MFA checklist could not be opened.
routes.fees_note: THB 10,000 baseline; embassy fees differ (USD 400 Washington, CHF 350 Bern). Funds of THB 500,000 are a balance, not income.
routes.physical_presence: Leave or extend every 180 days; tax residence at 180 days
routes.tax_note: Staying over 180 days in a year makes you Thai tax resident.

routes.name: Non-Immigrant O-X Long-Stay (retirement) visa, 10 years
routes.summary: Ten-year retirement visa for people aged 50+ from a list of eligible countries, with a Thai bank deposit.
routes.requirements: Age 50+, passport from an eligible country list (US, UK, Japan, Canada, Australia and most of Western Europe; list varies by embassy); either THB 3 million fixed deposit in a Thai bank, or THB 1.8 million deposit plus fixed annual income of THB 1.2 million (government page via search snippet); deposit held for the first year and at least THB 1.5 million kept thereafter; Thai health insurance of THB 400,000 inpatient and THB 40,000 outpatient. 5 years at a time, 10 in total; employment prohibited.
routes.investment_options: THB 3,000,000 fixed deposit; or THB 1,800,000 deposit plus THB 1,200,000 annual income.
routes.physical_presence: Report every 90 days; not stated otherwise
routes.tax_note: Staying over 180 days makes you tax resident.

routes.name: Thailand Privilege (Elite) membership
routes.summary: Paid membership that gives a long-stay visa of 5 to 20 years with concierge services, bought as a one-off fee.
routes.requirements: Membership by one-off fee: Bronze THB 650,000 (5 years, no points), Gold THB 900,000 (5 years), Platinum THB 1,500,000 (10 years), Diamond THB 2,500,000 (15 years), Reserve THB 5,000,000 (20 years, invitation only). Official page lists Bronze as available, but secondary guides report Bronze ending on 30 September 2026 or 31 December 2025; unconfirmed. Application fee (reported THB 50,000) and family fees not shown on the official page. Holders get a Special Tourist Visa and must report; membership gives no work right and no investment qualification.
routes.investment_options: Gold THB 900,000; Platinum THB 1,500,000; Diamond THB 2,500,000; Reserve THB 5,000,000 (invitation).
routes.fees_note: Membership fee is paid to the programme company, not a government fee.
routes.tax_note: Membership does not change tax residence (180 days).
